value.topic: Open Source Text-to-Speech (TTS) Models for Language Learning Addons
value.posting_intent: Seeking community recommendations and insights on reliable, multi-language open-source TTS models for a specific application, while also clarifying potential concerns.
value.speaker_role: community member seeking help with explicitly hypothetical product decision, not source author
value.current_user_goal: To find a suitable open-source TTS model for an Anki addon that generates audio for language learning flashcards, prioritizing local execution and multi-language support.
value.current_decision: Evaluating XTTS2 as a potential candidate but uncertain about its suitability due to perceived glitches and focus on voice cloning, and seeking alternatives.
value.desired_help: Recommendations for consistent and reliable open-source TTS models with strong multi-language support, and clarification on potential legal/ethical concerns regarding voice cloning and audio distribution for TTS models.
value.experimental_user_scenario: A developer is building an Anki addon for language learning and needs to integrate a local, free TTS model. They are considering XTTS2 but are hesitant due to its voice cloning focus and occasional glitches. They want to know if other models are more reliable and if there are any legal issues with using voice samples for cloning or distributing generated audio.
value.context: The user is developing an addon for Anki, an open-source flashcard software, to generate audio samples from flashcard content for language learning. The requirement is to use a local, open-source TTS model that does not rely on paid services or APIs, as existing free options are perceived to produce lower quality audio.

facts.text: The user is developing an addon for Anki, an open-source flashcard software.
facts.evidence_quote: I'm currently developing an addon for Anki (an open source flashcard software).

facts.text: The addon aims to generate audio samples from flashcard content for language learning.
facts.evidence_quote: One part of my plan is to integrate an option to generate audio samples based on the preexisting content of the flashcards (for language learning).

facts.text: The TTS model must be local and not require paid services or APIs.
facts.evidence_quote: The point of it is using a local TTS model that doesn't require any paid services or APIs.

facts.text: Existing free TTS addons for Anki are perceived to not generate good audio.
facts.evidence_quote: To my knowledge the addons that are currently available for this have no option for a free version that still generate quite good audio.

facts.text: XTTS2 is being considered due to broad language support and leaderboard evaluations, but is perceived as 'glitchy'.
facts.evidence_quote: My current bet would be XTTS2 due to the broad language support and its evaluation on leaderboards, but I find it to be a little "glitchy" at times.

facts.text: Concerns exist about XTTS2's focus on voice cloning and potential legal issues with distributing voice samples for cloning.
facts.evidence_quote: I don't know if it's a good pick because it's mostly focussed on voice cloning. Could that be an issue? Do I have to think about some sort of legal concerns When using such a model? Which voice samples am I allowed to distribute to people so they can be used for voice cloning?

facts.text: The user is seeking models that are consistent and reliable, with multi-language support.
facts.evidence_quote: Which models have you tested and which ones would you say are the most consistent and reliable?

limitations: The user cannot guarantee that users of the addon will be able to provide their own voice samples for cloning.
The addon must function locally without external paid services or APIs.
The TTS model needs to support multiple languages for language learning purposes.
allowed_claims: Open-source TTS models can be used for local audio generation.
Multi-language support is a key requirement for the TTS model.
Voice cloning capabilities of TTS models may raise legal or ethical questions.
Community members may have experience with various open-source TTS models and their reliability.
forbidden_claims: The user owns a specific piece of hardware for running TTS models.
The user has successfully implemented a TTS solution in their Anki addon.
The user has measured the performance or audio quality of any TTS model.
The user has personal experience with legal ramifications of voice cloning.
The user is asking for a definitive 'best' model without considering trade-offs.
